topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and introduces its learning objectives.

topics.label: Genetic foundations and determinants of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer as the evolution of mutation-bearing cells whose development depends on their biological circumstances.

topics.label: Environmental exposure and the interpretation of cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence that environmental exposures influence cancer risk rather than leaving its occurrence entirely to chance or inherited susceptibility.

topics.label: Infectious causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections contribute to carcinogenesis, with Burkitt lymphoma providing a detailed example.

topics.label: Mechanisms of DNA damage from environmental carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures produce DNA damage that can become cancer-associated mutations.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutation-bearing cells may require a growth-promoting environment before they develop into tumours.

topics.label: Carcinogen specificity and recap of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics consolidate how carcinogenic effects depend on the biological context in which exposure occurs.

topics.label: Investigating carcinogen exposure and carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how evidence linking exposures to cancer is generated and why that evidence has methodological limitations.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and placing them within everyday risk–benefit decisions.
